scope: measurement and explicit memory models; no engine changes
accounting: TPC-H published footprints retain existing padding; canonical sets use exact live keys+count when retained capacity is unobserved. DOOP owner totals and rigorous physical-sharing bounds are separate. Candidate codecs are estimates.

best.scope: sum of independently optimized per-query inventories

bitmap_cost_aware.scope: sum of independently optimized per-query inventories

best.scope: sum of independently optimized per-query inventories

bitmap_cost_aware.scope: sum of independently optimized per-query inventories

doop_physical_live_bounds.scope: immutable key buffers and their published metadata for all inventoried full layouts and both negative keysets; not allocator capacity, retained old snapshots, transient deltas, or query peak
doop_physical_live_bounds.basis: Rigorous source-derived bounds: admitted_orders builds one batch per relation/order and full_layouts clones it into same-order states. Each state merges independently, creating private merged buffers. Lower assumes maximum sharing within each order; upper counts IDB buffers independently but deduplicates EDB same-order buffers because EDB loading publishes once. Snapshot descriptors, counts and fields are distinct per layout. Both negative projections use one independently sorted run.

doop_semantic_remap_totals.scope: all 225 structures; optional shared rule-component dictionaries, each paid once; logical owner sum, not alias-deduplicated physical footprint
doop_semantic_remap_totals.basis: feasible conservative strategy enables all shared component maps, then chooses old no-remap best or component-product bitmap per structure; map cost is never free and original no-remap totals are retained
doop_semantic_remap_totals.selection_basis: exact enumeration of useful component-map subsets; charge each selected map once, collect a structure saving only if all required domains are mapped

methods.scope: Every index, rows/canonical publication and group declared in advised Structures; scan-only base inputs excluded. Canon policy and rows provider counted once. Per-query totals only.
methods.stats: Exact CPU relational evaluation over manifest binary files. Unknown means not successfully reconstructed; no synthetic cardinalities.
methods.current: Separate allocated and live scopes. RangeProvider reserves FOR slot capacity; SegmentedGroup retains 9*rows*arity+16 bytes. Canonical live scope uses generated packed word width*distinct rows+16-byte device metadata, with host schema descriptor bytes listed separately; retained pre-dedup capacities remain unknown.
methods.candidates: FOR1024 16-byte header plus u32 fence per block; bitmap rank every 512 positions; binary 65536 chunks choose uint16 array vs 8192-byte bitmap. Payload and bag occurrence endpoints retained.
methods.mapping: Equality-connected primary/foreign key columns share the full exported primary-key universe; other columns share their full exported source-column universe. Sparse numeric maps are separately charged sorted i64 value lists, once per shared domain per query; no private filtered-set interning.

totals.basis: Per-query sums, not suite co-residency. Live canonical storage includes distinct packed keys and device metadata but does not invent retained pre-dedup capacity. Host schema descriptors remain separate.

limitations: No GPU execution or new build: accepted advised plans and generated executors were available; CPU measurements use actual read-only binary exports.

Canonical retained pre-dedup capacities remain unknown. Their explicit live scope is generated packed word bytes times measured distinct rows plus 16-byte device OutputCount, retained by every candidate.
Physical pre-canon row counts cannot universally substitute for Sequence emission counts: membership compaction can remove join multiplicities before canonicalization.
Grouped publications retain all i64 aggregates and all validity bytes; candidates encode only lookup keys, never narrow aggregate values.
Raw-u32 and raw-FOR alternatives require no dense remapping. Separate dense-ranked alternatives charge measured shared-domain maps.

Current allocations are source-derived estimates, not allocator telemetry. Host object overhead, borrowed backing relations, shared count owners and sorting scratch are excluded; separately reported host schema descriptors are logical descriptor bytes.
All comparisons use identical per-query structure scopes; no summed query-suite value represents co-resident GPU memory.

Physical-prefix/flat-row raw-u32 and FOR candidates preserve every stored occurrence, begin/range-length arrays, recomputed offsets and20-byte metadata; they do not materialize logical expanded rows. FOR estimates assume an explicit lexicographic prefix permutation with aligned range metadata.
Grouped publications are sets keyed by distinct group keys with aggregate payload, not occurrence bags; bitmap-only storage cannot preserve that payload.

semantic_remap_totals.scope: all 225 structures; optional shared rule-component dictionaries, each paid once; logical owner sum, not alias-deduplicated physical footprint
semantic_remap_totals.basis: feasible conservative strategy enables all shared component maps, then chooses old no-remap best or component-product bitmap per structure; map cost is never free and original no-remap totals are retained
semantic_remap_totals.selection_basis: exact enumeration of useful component-map subsets; charge each selected map once, collect a structure saving only if all required domains are mapped

methods.layout_inventory: host compile of exact mini_engine source through stratify, incremental DeltaFirst, storage; device_storage preserves layout coverage/order by checked restoration
methods.input_identity: Facts::load deduplicates full rows; raw_fact_rows retains file occurrences. All emitted DOOP structures are sets, not bags.
methods.idb: 26 full GPU outputs; remaining acyclic IDBs evaluated as exact SQL projections/unions/joins of real facts using authored rules, checked against all available final GPU owner counts.
methods.symbols: Replay Method first, computed descriptors in BTreeMap/BTreeSet code order, then Facts load order; constants appended only if absent. No private per-set ranking.
methods.integer_dense_mapping: Optional shared integer-value rank map requires 8*distinct bytes once; plain/FOR use signed bias instead and require no mapping.
methods.mapping: Existing process-global IStr string dictionary is host-resident sunk/base mapping; GPU operates only on codes and has no string dictionary upload. Exact string bytes and estimated reverse-vector live bytes reported separately; hash capacity and allocator overhead unknown.
methods.bitmap: Raw-span product uses observed per-column min-relative integer spans and 4-byte base/8-byte span per coordinate; dense product uses the entire shared column universe per coordinate, never relation-private distinct ranks. Full tuple identity preserved; rank included in main bytes for position/count reads, membership-only bytes also recorded. Binary adaptive operates within each first-key group and shared second-column 2^16 chunks.
methods.bag: No bag structure in this DOOP plan. Bitmap alone would not preserve duplicate occurrences or attached payload in a bag.
methods.memory: Only immutable final per-structure data+descriptor ownership is compared. Candidate scratch, input host vectors, temporary deltas, string dictionaries and allocator cache are not silently mixed into those totals; relation aggregate allocated traces retained separately.

physical_live_bounds.scope: immutable key buffers and their published metadata for all inventoried full layouts and both negative keysets; not allocator capacity, retained old snapshots, transient deltas, or query peak
physical_live_bounds.basis: Rigorous source-derived bounds: admitted_orders builds one batch per relation/order and full_layouts clones it into same-order states. Each state merges independently, creating private merged buffers. Lower assumes maximum sharing within each order; upper counts IDB buffers independently but deduplicates EDB same-order buffers because EDB loading publishes once. Snapshot descriptors, counts and fields are distinct per layout. Both negative projections use one independently sorted run.
